properties.name: auth.service.url
properties.description: Base URL of the authentication service (e.g. http://localhost:8080).

properties.name: auth.service.api-key
properties.description: Shared secret injected as X-API-Key on internal service-to-service calls (e.g. C2B email validation). Must match AUTH_SERVICE_API_KEY on the auth service. Never used for user-facing Feign calls — those forward the caller's Bearer JWT instead.

properties.name: internal.api-key
properties.description: Shared secret internal services present via X-API-Key when calling wallet-service's /internal/** endpoints (see InternalApiKeyFilter). Must match property-service's app.api-key (INTERNAL_API_KEY env var) — both services read the same INTERNAL_API_KEY name, but from their own separate .env files.

properties.name: jwt.secret
properties.description: Base64-encoded secret key used to sign and verify JWT tokens. Must match across all services.

properties.name: rate-limit.requests-per-minute
properties.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute per client before rate limiting kicks in.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.consumer-key
properties.description: M-Pesa Daraja API consumer key.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.consumer-secret
properties.description: M-Pesa Daraja API consumer secret.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa business shortcode (paybill or till number).

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.passkey
properties.description: M-Pesa Lipa Na M-Pesa Online passkey used to generate the STK push password.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.callback-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL that Safaricom will POST STK push callbacks to. Use ngrok locally.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.environment
properties.description: Daraja environment to target: 'sandbox' for testing, 'production' for live.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.certificate-path
properties.description: Path to Safaricom's public X.509 certificate (.cer) used to RSA-encrypt initiator passwords into a SecurityCredential for B2C and B2B (see MpesaSecurityCredentialService). Bare paths (e.g. 'certs/SandboxCertificate.cer') resolve from the classpath — place files under src/main/resources/certs/. Prefix with 'file:' to load from an external path instead (e.g. a mounted secret). Sandbox and production use DIFFERENT certificate files.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa B2C API operator username used to initiate business-to-customer disbursements/payouts.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa B2C API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode that money is disbursed from in B2C transactions.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.command-id
properties.description: B2C transaction type: 'SalaryPayment', 'BusinessPayment', or 'PromotionPayment'.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the B2C request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final B2C transaction result to. This — not the initial paymentrequest response — is the actual source of truth for success/failure.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum KES amount accepted for a single B2C disbursement. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum KES amount accepted for a single B2C disbursement. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa B2B API operator username used to initiate business-to-business transfers.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa B2B API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode that funds move from (payer) in B2B transactions.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.receiver-shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa shortcode of the receiving organization in a B2B transaction.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.command-id
properties.description: B2B transaction type: 'BusinessPayBill', 'BusinessBuyGoods', or 'MerchantToMerchantTransfer'.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.sender-identifier-type
properties.description: Type of shortcode sending funds in a B2B transaction. 4 = organization shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.receiver-identifier-type
properties.description: Type of shortcode receiving funds in a B2B transaction. 4 = organization shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the B2B request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final B2B transaction result to. This — not the initial paymentrequest response — is the actual source of truth for success/failure. Note: B2B is a permissioned Safaricom API; confirm it's enabled for your shortcode before relying on it in production.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum KES amount accepted for a single B2B payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum KES amount accepted for a single B2B payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa business shortcode that C2B validation/confirmation URLs are registered against.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.response-type
properties.description: Default action Safaricom takes if the validation URL is unreachable: 'Completed' auto-accepts the payment, 'Cancelled' rejects it.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.validation-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls before completing a C2B payment, allowing the transaction to be accepted or rejected. Requires validation to be enabled on the shortcode via Safaricom support.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.confirmation-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs completed C2B payment details to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.express-checkout.receiver-shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa till shortcode being paid via B2B Express Checkout (USSD Push to Till). No initiator/security-credential needed — authenticated via the normal OAuth bearer token.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.express-checkout.partner-name
properties.description: Partner/organization name displayed to the merchant in the USSD PIN prompt during B2B Express Checkout.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.express-checkout.callback-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the B2B Express Checkout result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to top up a B2C shortcode's utility account from the working/MMF account (CommandID BusinessPayToBulk).

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.party-a
properties.description: M-Pesa B2C shortcode whose utility account is being topped up.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Account Top Up request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final Account Top Up result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to query the status of a prior transaction. Not yet wired to a service — reserved for automatic reconciliation of stuck B2C/B2B disbursements.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.party-a
properties.description: Shortcode or MSISDN that the transaction being queried belongs to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.identifier-type
properties.description: Type of organization receiving the transaction being queried. 1 = MSISDN, 2 = Till Number, 4 = Shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Transaction Status request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the Transaction Status query result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to query Working (MMF), Utility, and Charges Paid account balances for our own shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.party-a
properties.description: M-Pesa shortcode whose account balance is being queried.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.identifier-type
properties.description: Type of organization whose balance is being queried. 1 = MSISDN, 2 = Till Number, 4 = Shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Account Balance request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the Account Balance query result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to reverse a completed C2B transaction. Note: B2C payouts cannot be reversed via API — portal only.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.receiver-party
properties.description: M-Pesa shortcode that will be debited to refund the customer in a reversal.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.receiver-identifier-type
properties.description: Type of organization identified by receiver-party for a reversal. Must be 11 per Safaricom's spec.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Reversal request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final Reversal result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to pay directly into a customer's Pochi la Biashara business wallet. Requires a B2C shortcode capable of both receiving and disbursing.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.party-a
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode that money is disbursed from in B2Pochi transactions.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the B2Pochi request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final B2Pochi transaction result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum KES amount accepted for a single B2Pochi payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum KES amount accepted for a single B2Pochi payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode whose C2B transactions are being pulled for reconciliation.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.nominated-number
properties.description: The Safaricom MSISDN tied to this shortcode's KYC, found on the M-PESA portal — not something you choose arbitrarily. Required for the Pull Transactions API.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.callback-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs pulled transaction batches to. Unlike every other operational M-Pesa API above, Pull Transactions needs NO initiator name/password/SecurityCredential — just the OAuth bearer token, same as STK Push and C2B Register URL.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.pull-days
properties.description: Default lookback window (in days) when a query doesn't specify its own dates. Maximum of 2, since Safaricom only retains 48 hours of pullable transaction data.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.offset-value
properties.description: Number of records to skip in the pull transactions result set, used for pagination.

properties.name: stripe.secret-key
properties.description: Stripe secret API key (sk_test_* for sandbox, sk_live_* for production). Found in the Stripe Dashboard under Developers → API keys.

properties.name: stripe.webhook-secret
properties.description: Stripe platform webhook signing secret (whsec_*) — verifies /payments/stripe/webhook (deposits, saved cards). Found in Stripe Dashboard → Webhooks → your platform endpoint → Signing secret. Distinct from stripe.connect.webhook-secret below, which is a separate destination for events on connected accounts.

properties.name: stripe.connect.refresh-url
properties.description: Frontend URL Stripe redirects the user to if their Connect onboarding link expired, was already used, or is otherwise invalid. The frontend should request a fresh link (POST /wallet/stripe/connect/link) and redirect again from there.

properties.name: stripe.connect.return-url
properties.description: Frontend URL Stripe redirects the user to after finishing or exiting Connect onboarding. Reaching this URL does not guarantee onboarding fully succeeded — the frontend should call POST /wallet/stripe/connect/refresh or GET /wallet/stripe/connect/account to confirm actual status.

properties.name: stripe.connect.webhook-secret
properties.description: Stripe Connect webhook signing secret (whsec_*) — verifies /payments/stripe/connect/webhook (account.updated, payout.paid, payout.failed on connected accounts). Created as a SEPARATE destination from stripe.webhook-secret above via Dashboard → Webhooks → new destination → 'Listen to events on Connected accounts' — Stripe does not deliver connected-account events to the platform webhook's destination.

properties.name: paypal.client-id
properties.description: PayPal REST API client ID. Found in the PayPal Developer Dashboard under your app credentials.

properties.name: paypal.client-secret
properties.description: PayPal REST API client secret. Found in the PayPal Developer Dashboard under your app credentials.

properties.name: paypal.environment
properties.description: PayPal environment to target: 'sandbox' for testing, 'production' for live.

properties.name: paypal.webhook-id
properties.description: PayPal Webhook ID from the Developer Dashboard, used to verify that incoming /payments/paypal/webhook requests genuinely came from PayPal (see PaypalService.verifyWebhookSignature). Register your endpoint (https://<your-domain>/payments/paypal/webhook) under your app's Webhooks section to obtain this. If left blank, webhook verification fails closed and all incoming PayPal webhooks are rejected.

properties.name: paypal.return-url
properties.description: URL PayPal redirects the customer to after approving an order that requires a separate approval step (no saved/vaulted payment source, or a saved source that needs re-authorization).

properties.name: paypal.cancel-url
properties.description: URL PayPal redirects the customer to if they cancel out of order approval instead of completing it.

properties.name: flutterwave.client-id
properties.description: Flutterwave v4 OAuth2 client_credentials client ID. Replaces v3's static Secret Key/Public Key model entirely — v4 has no 'public key'. Found in the Flutterwave Dashboard under API keys.

properties.name: flutterwave.client-secret
properties.description: Flutterwave v4 OAuth2 client_credentials client secret, used with flutterwave.client-id to obtain access tokens from the OAuth2 token endpoint (see FlutterwaveService.getAccessToken).

properties.name: flutterwave.encryption-key
properties.description: Flutterwave encryption key, found in the Flutterwave Dashboard alongside your API keys.

properties.name: flutterwave.environment
properties.description: Flutterwave environment to target: 'sandbox' or 'production'. Unlike v3, this DOES determine the base URL (see FlutterwaveConfig.baseUrl()) — sandbox and production are genuinely different hosts, not just different key prefixes on one URL.

properties.name: flutterwave.webhook-secret-hash
properties.description: Arbitrary shared-secret string configured in the Flutterwave Dashboard (Settings → Webhooks → Secret Hash). Used as the HMAC-SHA256 key to verify the 'flutterwave-signature' header on incoming /payments/flutterwave/webhook requests (see FlutterwaveService.verifyWebhookSignature) — NOT a plain string comparison the way v3's 'verif-hash' worked.

properties.name: flutterwave.redirect-url
properties.description: URL Flutterwave redirects the customer to after completing a charge's authorization step (3DS, mobile money approval, etc.).

properties.name: flutterwave.sandbox-scenario-key
properties.description: SANDBOX TESTING ONLY. When set, every write call to Flutterwave carries this value as the 'X-Scenario-Key' header, forcing a deterministic mock outcome (e.g. 'scenario:successful', 'scenario:failed', 'scenario:auth_redirect') instead of default sandbox behavior. Leave unset in production — sending this against the live API is rejected or ignored depending on endpoint, and its presence in production config is a signal something is misconfigured.

properties.name: flutterwave.transfer.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum amount accepted for a single Flutterwave transfer (bank or mobile money disbursement). Confirm actual tier limits with Flutterwave for your account.

properties.name: flutterwave.transfer.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum amount accepted for a single Flutterwave transfer (bank or mobile money disbursement). Confirm actual tier limits with Flutterwave for your account.

properties.name: flutterwave.transfer.source-currency
properties.description: The currency your Flutterwave balance actually holds — used as payment_instruction.source_currency on every payout. NOT automatically the same as the destination currency the recipient receives in. Confirm your actual settlement/balance currency in the Flutterwave dashboard before relying on this in production.

properties.name: nowpayments.base-url
properties.description: NOWPayments API host. Sandbox and production are genuinely separate hosts with separate accounts/keys, not just different key prefixes on one URL — 'https://api-sandbox.nowpayments.io' for testing, 'https://api.nowpayments.io' for production. No trailing slash.

properties.name: nowpayments.api-key
properties.description: NOWPayments API key, sent as the 'x-api-key' header on every request. Found in Dashboard → Settings → Payments → API keys. Requires at least one wallet added under Payout wallets before a key can be generated.

properties.name: nowpayments.ipn-secret
properties.description: Verifies the 'x-nowpayments-sig' header on incoming IPN webhooks (see NowPaymentsService.verifyIpnSignature) — HMAC-SHA512 over the recursively-key-sorted JSON body. Found in Dashboard → Settings → Payments → Instant payment notifications. NOT the same value as nowpayments.api-key above, and NOT interchangeable between sandbox/production.

properties.name: nowpayments.callback-url
properties.description: Your own public HTTPS URL for /payments/nowpayments/webhook, sent as ipn_callback_url on every Create Payment request. No sandbox tunnel/CLI tooling exists here the way Stripe CLI's 'stripe listen' does — this needs to be a real reachable URL (e.g. via zrok/ngrok in dev) even while testing in sandbox.

properties.name: nowpayments.payout-email
properties.description: Your NOWPayments DASHBOARD LOGIN email — NOT the same thing as nowpayments.api-key, and a meaningfully more sensitive secret. Required only for payouts: obtains a short-lived JWT via POST /v1/auth (see NowPaymentsService.getAuthToken), needed in addition to the x-api-key header every other call uses. Deposits never touch this.

properties.name: nowpayments.payout-password
properties.description: Your NOWPayments DASHBOARD LOGIN password — paired with nowpayments.payout-email above for the same POST /v1/auth call. Treat this with real secrets-management discipline, more so than a typical API key — whoever holds it can log into the dashboard directly, not just make scoped API calls.

properties.name: commission.internal-transfer-rate
properties.description: Commission rate taken on internal wallet-to-wallet transfers (POST /wallet/transfer, POST /internal/transfer) — a decimal fraction, e.g. 0.01 for 1%, not 1. Expected lower than commission.gateway-rate, matching real payment-processing economics (an internal transfer costs nothing external, unlike a gateway withdrawal).

properties.name: commission.gateway-rate
properties.description: Commission rate taken on gateway-bound disbursements (M-Pesa B2C/B2Pochi, PayPal, Stripe, Flutterwave, NOWPayments) — a decimal fraction, e.g. 0.03 for 3%, not 3. Expected higher than commission.internal-transfer-rate, roughly in line with typical real-world gateway processing fees.

properties.name: frontend.url
properties.description: Frontend application URL used for CORS allowed-origins configuration.

properties.name: notifications.b2b-recipients
properties.description: Comma-separated admin/finance email addresses notified on every B2B success/failure (see MpesaDisbursementService.notifyB2BRecipients). B2B never touches a customer wallet, so there's no wallet owner's email to notify the way B2C/B2Pochi have — this is who gets it instead. Whitespace around commas is trimmed. Left empty/unset is safe: logs a warning and sends no email, never throws.

properties.name: exchange-rate.refresh-interval-ms
properties.description: How often (in milliseconds) ExchangeRateService's scheduled job re-fetches every previously-saved currency pair from Frankfurter and refreshes the Redis/MongoDB cache. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation itself via this same property placeholder, not through a properties class at annotation-processing time — kept in sync with the same default (20 minutes) regardless.

properties.name: exchange-rate.max-retries
properties.description: Maximum retry attempts ExchangeRateService's scheduled refresh makes per currency pair before giving up on that pair for the current refresh cycle and moving on to the next.
